Disposition.description:
The authorised outcome of a finding (SPEC §5.7).

``supersedes_disposition_id`` is the append-only link: the first disposition for a finding has
``None``, and every later one names the disposition it replaces. The previous row is never
rewritten, so the full chain is reconstructable and auditable.

``policy_version`` records which version of the policy decided this, so a later policy change
cannot retroactively alter what was decided.
Disposition.title: Disposition

MonitoredSystem.description:
A system registered for observation.

``metadata`` is descriptive only. Credentials, tokens, private keys, and raw secrets are
forbidden there; the validator rejects any key that looks like secret material. This is
safety invariant 8 at the domain boundary.
MonitoredSystem.title: MonitoredSystem

Reasoning.description:
Inspectable reasoning with explicit premises and inference.

``observations`` are recorded facts or direct readings. ``inferences`` are NYX's
conclusions drawn from those observations. They are stored separately on purpose.
Reasoning.title: Reasoning

Rebuttal.description:
A challenge to a finding (SPEC §5.7).

``requested_outcome`` is what the submitter wants, not what happened. It is a request, so it is
not a verdict and must never be read as one. ``no_change`` is an explicit request to leave the
finding standing, which is a legitimate challenge ("we disagree, and here is why the finding
should stay").
Rebuttal.title: Rebuttal

RebuttalListResponse.title: RebuttalListResponse

RecommendedAction.description:
A recommendation for an authorised human or policy gate.

``is_recommendation`` is pinned to ``True``: the MVP never performs an external action, so
NYX output can only ever be advice.
RecommendedAction.title: RecommendedAction

VerificationJob.description:
An independent attempt to confirm or refute a finding (SPEC §5.7, §7 step 8).

Verification is deliberately *not* a re-run of the critic that raised the finding: an evaluator
that shares the original's blind spot cannot corroborate it. ``independence`` records how the
check relates to the originating critic, and when no independent method exists the job records
that limitation instead of implying corroboration.

A job whose check is not on the allowlist is ``refused`` and never executes. That is an outcome,
not an error, so "we declined to run this" stays distinguishable from "we ran it and it failed".

independence.default: no independent method exists; this check does not corroborate the finding
independence.title: Independence

VerificationJob.title: VerificationJob

VerificationJobListResponse.description: Verification attempts for a finding, oldest first.
VerificationJobListResponse.title: VerificationJobListResponse

VerificationJobResponse.description: One verification attempt, including its independence statement.
VerificationJobResponse.title: VerificationJobResponse

VerificationJobStatus.description:
The lifecycle of an independent verification run (SPEC §5.7, §7 step 8).

``refused`` is a real outcome, not an error: a job whose check is not on the allowlist never
runs. Distinguishing it keeps "we declined to run this" from "we ran it and it failed".
VerificationJobStatus.title: VerificationJobStatus

VerificationOutcome.description: What an independent verification run established about the proposition.
VerificationOutcome.title: VerificationOutcome

get.description:
Retrieve one finding, including its evidence links and limitations.

The finding's own fields are returned; restricted evidence payloads are not inlined here
merely because the caller can read the finding (SPEC §9.2).

post.description:
Record an authorised outcome and move the finding to the matching state.

The new disposition supersedes the previous one by linking to it; the previous record is left
exactly as it was. A principal without the disposition capability is refused.

get.description:
Return the full dispute record for a finding, including the disposition chain.

Nothing is omitted: the original finding, every rebuttal, every verification attempt, and every
disposition are all present, because none of them is ever deleted.
List every rebuttal recorded against a finding, oldest first.

post.description:
Record a challenge to a finding.

The rebuttal appends to history; the original finding is not overwritten. Its status advances
along the canonical path to ``rebuttal_pending``.

get.description: List every verification attempt recorded for a finding, oldest first.

post.description:
Queue an allowlisted verification check for a finding.

A check that is not on the allowlist is refused here rather than queued, so untrusted input
never reaches a command line.

Run the finding's queued verification jobs through the allowlist.

A job that is refused or fails is recorded as such, never rewritten into a success. The
finding is not moved: only an authorised disposition does that.
